descriptionChirho: Piel stem: to stir up or incite others to action, a causative/transitive sense. Cross-linguistic evidence consistently uses causative vocabulary: eng 'stirs up', spa 'suscita', hin 'भड़काता', arb 'يُثِيرُ', kor '일으키다', swa 'huchochea/anachochea'.

Hitpael reflexive/reciprocal: to provoke oneself against, engage in strife, contend with someone. Cross-linguistic evidence uses general hostility/provocation vocabulary: eng 'provoke/contend/stir up strife', spa 'te metas/te provocas/te enfrentaste/contenderán', hin 'भड़काओ/उकसाओगे/लड़ाई ली/लड़ते', arb 'تَتَحَرَّشْ/تَسْتَثِيرُ/تَتَحَدَّى/يُقاوِمُونَ', kor '싸우라/도발하느냐/다투다', swa 'usiwachokoe/unajichokoza/hupigana'.

Hitpael with specifically military meaning: to wage war, prepare for battle, engage in armed conflict. Distinguished from general 'provoke/contend' by consistent military vocabulary across all languages: spa 'se preparará para guerra', hin 'युद्ध करेगा/करेंगे' (war), arb 'يَتَحَرَّشُ/يَتَحَرَّشُونَ', swa 'ataandaa vita/wataandaa vita' (prepare for war), kor '싸우리라'.
